newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross still trying to set up talks in Lima.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross still trying to set up talks in Lima.

text.p: Red Cross mediators said on Saturday they were still trying to set up negotiations between the Peruvian government and Marxist rebels holding hundreds of hostages in the Japanese ambassador's home for four days.

"We consider this crisis, and hopeful negotiation, is still in its initial phase," spokesman Roland Bigler told Reuters. "The initial phase is made up of contributing to establishing communications between the government and the rebels."
Asked whether this meant the Red Cross had not set up any channel between the rebels and the government, Bigler said:
"We are trying to establish the links."

He added that he did not know whether communications had been established through any other mediator. The Peruvian government has said the Red Cross are the only recognized mediators for solving the crisis.
When asked if the government had passed a message or instruction to the rebels, Bigler said: "To my knowledge there has been no message or instruction from the government."

Another Red Cross official involved in negotiations, who asked not to be named, said the fact that "a physical link exists in and out of the compound (to bring in supplies) is an important first step of opening the premises and establishing communication links. It has shown the barrier can be brought down."
